answer: Sybils get expensive when payment demands a sky no script can fake. Each seat is pinned to one one-degree cell and must post a fresh plate of that nebula per settlement: latitude in peak altitude, longitude in when that peak meets local noon, so no city can pose as another. Emulsion fogs in weeks; nothing stockpiles. A lab seals each under an ivory bead stamped with its cell, on sable-dyed cord that snaps if opened. A thousand wallets mean a thousand clear nights, a thousand cells and a thousand fees, while each seat earns the same: per-identity cost stays flat and the farm loses money.
